gap: No result ChatGPT got states that TESSAN's TC03 converter tops out at 250 W and is meant for phones, tablets and cameras, while TESSAN's other converter combo has a separate 2,000 W converter area that it says is for hair dryers, straighteners and curling irons. That split is the converter-to-device pairing behind ChatGPT's line that hair dryers 'may require a voltage converter'.
standout_why: I compared against packandporter.com, universaltraveladapter.net (TESSAN-branded), thefinerroute.com and nbcnews.com Select. Pack & Porter only says to leave a 110 V dryer at home. universaltraveladapter.net says the adapters are 'not a voltage converter' and names no converter model. NBC lists the Foval converter at 230 W, which a US dryer exceeds. The Finer Route names no converter. None of them pairs a converter model with its device class or wattage cap. Several pages already cover the plug-type mapping (Type C for continental Europe, G for UK/Ireland, J for Switzerland, L for Italy). The Finer Route says 'Slim Type C usually fits' in Switzerland, and Pack & Porter says a Type J socket 'will accept a slim Type C plug but not a Schuko Type F one'. So plug-fit facts alone would score 0–1.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's pick of an adapter only for continental Europe (Ceptics CTU-9C, Type C). It changes the answer for anyone bringing a single-voltage US hair tool. The TC03 (250 W, which TESSAN pitches at phones, tablets and cameras) is the wrong buy for that. Only a converter with a ~2,000 W stage, like TESSAN's 4-USB converter combo, matches what TESSAN itself names for dryers. A price fix also matters: Ceptics' own store lists the CTU-9C at $9.99, not the $17.99 ChatGPT showed. On the same store, $17.99 is the C + E/F 'European Combo' (CTU-9-9C), and the Swiss combo carries the same price. The Swiss (Type J, CTU-9C-11A) and Italy (Type L, CTU-12-9C) combos both show out of stock, so for those trips a Type C unit or a universal model is what you can actually buy.
